name: San Diego
tagline: Perfect Weather, Beach Living, and Laid-Back California Vibes
description: San Diego offers arguably the best climate in the United States, with year-round sunshine and mild temperatures that rarely dip below 50°F. The city blends world-class beaches, a thriving craft beer scene, and proximity to the Mexican border for affordable day trips. While California taxes and housing costs are real headwinds for FIRE retirees, the quality of life and outdoor lifestyle are hard to beat anywhere in the country.

quickFacts.visa: No visa required for US citizens
quickFacts.safetyRating: Moderate – safe by large US city standards
quickFacts.climate: Subtropical Mediterranean with warm, dry summers and mild winters

housing.description: An older studio or 1BR inland in City Heights, El Cajon, or Clairemont, where the studio floor sets a hard bottom

dining.description: Home cooking plus San Diego's cheap, excellent fish tacos and Mexican food

healthcare.description: Covered California individual plan with a premium tax credit at a MAGI kept under the cliff (plus a modest CA state subsidy); a sticky post-subsidy floor. Assumes an early retiree (45–55); older retirees budget more.

transportation.description: A paid-off used car with CA insurance and gas — essential in a metro with weak transit outside downtown

entertainment.description: Free and constant recreation — the beaches, Balboa Park, and the Torrey Pines trails

1M.lifestyle: A careful but sun-soaked Southern California life. Housing is an older studio or 1BR inland in City Heights, El Cajon, or Clairemont, where the studio floor sets a hard bottom. A paid-off used car is essential in a metro with weak transit outside downtown, and it anchors the budget alongside a subsidized marketplace health plan. Meals lean on home cooking and San Diego's cheap, excellent fish tacos and Mexican food. Recreation is free and constant — the beaches, Balboa Park, and the Torrey Pines trails — under reliably mild weather year-round.

3M.lifestyle: A comfortable coastal-city life in a one-bedroom in a desirable neighborhood like North Park, Hillcrest, or Point Loma. Dining out regularly at the city's strong mid-range restaurants and breweries, a newer car, and standing outdoor pursuits — surfing, sailing, golf at Torrey Pines — become the routine. A solid private health plan and weekend trips to Anza-Borrego or across the border to Baja round it out. California taxes take a cut, but the year-round climate makes outdoor living a daily default.

10M.lifestyle: Top-of-market San Diego living, anchored by a luxury 2-bedroom in a coastal or downtown high-rise near La Jolla, Coronado, or the waterfront. A private chef, a luxury car, full household help, and concierge medicine at Scripps or UCSD are routine, alongside first-class travel and standing memberships at the city's sailing and golf clubs. The mild coastal climate means outdoor living every day, and the budget supports entertaining and dining without a second thought — established wealth in one of the country's best climates.
